title: Stochasticity and probabilistic trajectory scoring are essential for data-driven closures of chaotic systems
summary: Coarse-grained models of chaotic systems neglect unresolved degrees of freedom, inducing structured model error that limits predictability and distorts long-term statistics. Typical data-driven closures are trained to minimize error over a single time step, implicitly assuming Markovian dynamics and often failing to capture long-term behavior. Recent approaches instead optimize losses over finite trajectories.
